studies.title: Budgetary Equilibrium & Need vs Want Allocation
studies.summary: Need expenditure represents core baseline staples. Want expenditure represents discretionary lifestyle choices.
studies.advice: Keep Needs as the majority share (>50%) of total spend. When Wants exceed Needs, evaluate upcoming purchases with a 24-hour delay.

studies.title: Real-Time Micro-Transaction Friction
studies.citation: NotebookLM Section 3.1 — Real-Time Friction Behavioral Control
studies.summary: Impulse purchases occur when transaction friction is zero. Real-time categorization forces active decision making.
studies.advice: Always log purchases immediately at point-of-sale to preserve behavioral friction and habit reinforcement.

studies.title: Compensatory Budget Recovery
studies.summary: Overspending on a single day should be compensated by tightening discretionary Want spending on subsequent days.
studies.advice: If you exceed your daily budget today, reduce your daily Want target by 33% for the next 3 days until liquidity normalizes.
